analysis.title: Correction, not yet contagion
key_insights: Nasdaq 100 is about 11% below its recent high (11.2% currently, peak drawdown 14.7% on 5 Nov) while the S&P 500 is roughly 4% below its peak. Historically broader risk-off episodes see the two drawdowns converge, so the persistent gap indicates the correction is concentrated in former Technology leadership.

Breadth: Technology participation has deteriorated sharply, but around 65-70% of S&P 500 constituents remain above their 50-day moving average. Pictet reads this as a reset in former leadership, not broad-based deterioration.

The Nasdaq 100 peaked at 31,225 on 6 Oct 2026 and entered correction territory 19 sessions later, on 2 Nov, at 27,990 (10.4% below the peak). That is fast but slower than the 2020 COVID sell-off (3 sessions), several dot-com episodes (5-7 sessions) and the 1987 crash (9 sessions).

After the Nasdaq first falls 10%, average and median returns rise over time and the share of negative outcomes falls from about 45% initially to about 30% after two months. The current episode has lagged the typical early recovery and sits close to its initial 10% correction level.

Historically recession has not changed the size of an ordinary S&P 500 correction (average drawdown about 14% with or without recession). Beyond the first 10%, recessionary episodes were far more likely to deepen: 60% reached -20%, 40% reached -30% and 30% reached -40%, versus 33%, 17% and 0% without recession.
Median time from the first -10% drawdown to the trough was 10.5 months in recessionary episodes versus one month without recession.

Macro transmission is not evident: the Citi US Economic Surprise Index remains strongly positive, and Pictet's Macro Momentum Model recovered to about 60-65% as of the 30 Sep update (October reading incomplete, housing and PMI pending).

Earnings do not confirm the sell-off: 12M forward S&P 500 EPS estimates have kept rising to about $417 and the Earnings Revision Ratio is positive and rising, so Pictet reads the move as valuation compression rather than earnings deterioration. Post-report price reactions are more volatile, with less tolerance for weak guidance, margin pressure and heavy capital intensity.
Warning signs that would indicate contagion: ERR falling below zero, forward EPS expectations weakening, softer economic data, and wider credit spreads. None is present now.

Sentiment has reset sharply: the AAII bull-bear spread is firmly negative while the S&P 500 is near its high and above its rising 200-day average. Bearish sentiment alone is not a bottom signal, but it has deteriorated further than the fundamentals.

Options: 1M ATM implied vol is about 15.4 (71st percentile) and 3M about 16.3 (68th percentile). Put/call skew is mid-range and the Option Fear Gauge is below peaks of prior severe stress, indicating repricing of risk without indiscriminate stress.

S&P 500 technicals: rebound from the 7,350 low toward the rising 200-day SMA at 7,331. Resistance is 7,629-7,656; a sustained move above 7,656 targets 7,716 and the 7,845 high. Support is 7,500, then 7,437 and 7,350-7,331.

sector_views.rationale: Technology leadership is where the correction is concentrated and participation has deteriorated sharply, but Pictet sees a reset in former leadership rather than a macro or earnings-driven breakdown.

earnings_insights: 12M forward S&P 500 EPS estimates have risen to about $417 (estimate, per FactSet) even as prices fell.

The latest earnings season aggregate results are described as solid, with more volatile post-report price reactions and less tolerance for weaker guidance, margin pressure and elevated capital intensity.
The Earnings Revision Ratio is positive and has recently turned higher, so analysts are making more upward than downward revisions. A reading below zero would be the warning sign.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Data are beating consensus, so there is no sign of macro deterioration alongside the Nasdaq correction. The index measures outcomes against expectations, not the absolute level of growth.
Recovered materially from its 2024-25 lows and moved away from weak-momentum readings tied to recession risk. The October reading is incomplete (housing and PMI pending).
Estimates keep rising while prices fall, which points to valuation compression rather than earnings deterioration.

risk_factors: Spread of the correction beyond Technology, with the S&P 500 drawdown converging toward the Nasdaq's.
Softer economic data, negative earnings revisions (ERR below zero, falling forward EPS) and wider credit spreads would make the weakness structural.
Renewed Nasdaq weakness would move the episode toward the less favourable part of the historical post-correction distribution.
Investors are less tolerant of weaker guidance, margin pressure and elevated capital intensity at earnings.
A break below 7,500 on the S&P 500 would weaken the recovery, with 7,437 and 7,350-7,331 as the next support.

tension_points.bull_case: Macro and earnings are not confirming the sell-off: the Citi Economic Surprise Index is strongly positive, the Macro Momentum Model is at 60-65%, forward S&P 500 EPS is about $417 and rising, and the ERR is positive. About 65-70% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 50-day average, so the move looks like a reset in former tech leadership.
tension_points.bear_case: The Nasdaq has lagged the typical post-10% recovery path and sits near its initial correction level, and implied vol is in the 71st percentile. Historically, recessionary corrections deepen (60% reached -20%) and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq drawdowns tend to converge in broad risk-off episodes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The ERR falling below zero with forward EPS expectations weakening, softer economic data and wider credit spreads, or an S&P 500 break below 7,500.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Tech-led correction has not been matched by deterioration in macro data or earnings, so it looks like a reset in leadership rather than broad risk-off.
theme_stances.evidence: Tech weakness has yet to be matched by deterioration in the macro and earnings backdrop
